In October of 2020, the record shows us converging. Fifty-one of us said "paycheck protection program"; another 47 said "the paycheck protection program" — one program, entering our mouths two ways on the same peak day. Fifty of us said "updated heroes act," 46 said "the updated heroes," 44 said "the updated heroes act," and 48 reached back to "the heroes act." We were, that month, largely one relief bill spoken in variations.

Then, late in the month, the count shifted. On October 26, 47 of us said "the supreme court" and 47 of us said "amy coney barrett" — the same figure, the same day, a second script arriving as the first receded.

We note that "updated heroes act" first appears in our record from Steve Cohen, and "the paycheck protection program" from James A. Himes. The rest we said together, and in these numbers.
